Assassin’s Creed Origins stands out for its beautiful recreation of Ancient Egypt, from vast deserts to lively cities like Alexandria. The world feels immersive and historically rich. Bayek’s voice acting is excellent and adds real emotional depth to the story.

At the time of its release, Assassin’s Creed Origins was a polarizing title. However, as newer releases came out, Origins made more sense in its position as a better game overall for me. It offers a great story, great pacing, and a “just right” amount of content to keep you exploring further (compared to the newer ones, anyway).

The system changes are understandable for it to become a fully fledged Open World RPG experience. The OG systems are designed to be a semi-linear and "consumable" experience, and it's still one of the best for it.

Overall, it provides a great experience of what the Assassin’s Creed series could develop into, excluding a focus on microtransactions, which the newer ones seem to prioritize (e.g., lengthening the game, level walls, etc.).

Great open world, so much content you'll probably never finish the game without a whole lot of trying. The scenery is breathtaking, the sounds enamoring, and the actions of your targets truly outrageous and angering. I don't think that I've felt so personally furious and immersed in a game's storyline in a long time. Bayek is an extremely likable character with enormous charisma; his interactions with children is truly heartwarming. Last but certainly not least, the character design of so many of your enemies will make you wish you got to see more of them before you put an end to them. My main complaint is that the horses look pretty terrible and have weird triangle necks - but I'm coming at this from 2021, having been spoilt by RDR2, so that's not a very fair comparison!

This AAA game is now the newest of the Assassin's Creed series.This is the oldest story in the whole series. The plot will take player to the Ptolemaic Kingdom. And Ptolemy XIII (Cleopatra VII rules) is the last king of the Ptolemaic Kingdom.

What an incredible experience! I really appreciated the story and, more than anything, the feeling of actually living in Ancient Egypt. The world, atmosphere, characters and historical setting made the journey feel immersive from beginning to end.

There is something truly special about the way this game brings Ancient Egypt to life. Walking through the deserts, exploring ancient cities, temples, tombs, villages and seeing the Nile stretching across the horizon made me feel like I had stepped into another time. It wasn’t just a world I was exploring, it felt like a world I was living in. Every place seemed to carry its own history, mystery and story.

The story itself made that experience even more meaningful. The emotions, struggles, relationships and personal journey of the characters gave the world a heart. There were moments when I completely forgot that I was playing a game and simply became lost in the journey. That feeling of being connected to the world is something I will genuinely remember.

This is the first Assassin’s Creed game I’ve ever finished and honestly, it feels like the perfect starting point for my Assassin’s Creed journey. After experiencing Origins, I finally understand why this series has meant so much to so many players.

Origins didn’t just give me a great game to play. It gave me a world to explore, a story to experience and a journey that I’ll carry with me as I continue through the series.

''This is where my Assassin’s Creed journey begins.''

Nothing much to say except; this was magnificent. AC wasn't always my favourite game series, I've only ever finished Black Flag and Rogue, but this one grabbed me right from the beginning and gripped me right til the end. I put an insane amount of time into this game, into getting 100% completion (those final two achievements will forever bug me though) and it was a hell of an experience.

Jaw-droppingly gorgeous, fantastic VA, engrossing story, fabulous combat system, and an enormous world to explore and discover.

This was fantastic and if it truly had any downsides it would be the shocking sys-abuse it had. CPU usage was off the charts, for no good reason, and had near constant stutter/hitching during cutscenes, as well as frequent performance drops in towns. That's a shame, and even though I was eventually able to eke out a fairly constant 60fps (town traversal notwithstanding with the terrible framepacing and the frequent drops to 40s and 50s) on my 4.3Ghz 3770K, 16GB RAM, and a GTX1070 OC'd to 2Ghz, it should still be improved significantly IMO. I can imagine people on lesser systems being seriously frustrated and having to cap framerate to 30 just to get a decent experience.

I wholehearted recommend the game to anyone who loves AC, anyone who loves great stories, and anyone who gets a kick out of huge open worlds.

Being an open world enthusiast I have loved, admired, disliked and even hated countless pieces belonging to this genre, with all my being, just for my sheer deep rooted love for the vast possibilities of world building and biome design that revolves around this genre and this genre only. But only have I worshipped one amongst them all and it is Assassin's Creed Origins. Besides owning a physical collector's edition of this game, I own gold editions throughout multiple digital distribution platforms. So yeah at this point the only thing keeping this game from being a full fledged religion is me not waging a war in it's name. Yet I've always failed to successfully construct a proper review letting people know about what I love about the game and what I don't, for 8 years now. So is the tragedy of ineffable love, I guess. But fret not, as today's not any special, it's just after experiencing the ever so beautifully done biome designs of Crimson Desert, I could not help but wonder - would it be possible today if not for the pinnacle of biome designing that came before?

I haven't played many of the games in the series overall. I really only ever 100% 2 on 360 as a teenager. Played a bit of Syndicate when I got it on sale awhile ago but kinda lost interest so I dropped it before finishing up the main story. I launched odyssey once to get access to 3 but honestly just didn't like the characters in that one so dropped it too, Playing through this one all the way through main story + both dlcs I like it overall. Sure the RPG aspects and stealth stuff felt more optional then the last ones but I actually though the combat was a little refreshing instead of just "hit one button to parry" the game. I enjoyed all the choices I had with weaponry and tools at my disposal. Only real gripe I had was that some part of the game were a bit grindy, requiring side quest/hidden quests to keep up with level and gear upgrades. I really like Bayek as an MC and wish he got more notice outside of this game because the story between him and Aya is both good and also bittersweet af. I plan on playing through Odyssey next then Valhalla after. I'll get Mirage eventually when it pops on steam with a fat enough discount so I feel less bad about giving Ubisoft some pocket change.

Assassin's Creed® Origins is the GREAT game for me. First of all I like the old story about Egypt, the map is big and beautiful there is a lot to explore. The missions are not difficult, at least for me, I like that there is a lot of space to explore. It doesn't take long to reach at least 40 levels, at least I like the obtaining XP for any each new location and for almost everything you get a certain amount of XP. I also like the weapons you get from the mission, and from the loots. The only thing I don't like is that something has to go over HEXA Chest. I also don’t like how money is raised in the game, slow a lot. I like that there are animals in the game, and I don't like how TAMED was done, after restarting the game you don't have that animal. Sometimes I don’t like movement in the game. The bayak is sometimes coiled and moves slowly. I also like how much space there is for Fast Travel.

But in the game, I convincingly like the story of that ancient Egypt and the maps the most.

The textures of the map are perfect, but you also have good PC.. Textures on low for low PC are still good.

I like the game and I will always play it. I have to emphasize that the game sometimes reminds me of Far Cry Primal.
